answer: Memory-hard sequential proofs binds each identity to a RAM-bound verifiable delay function computed per identity. An attacker needs 2 dedicated RAM modules per clone, so a 1,000-clone farm needs 2,000 separate allocations. The network enforces this via spot-checked delay-function outputs every epoch. The ripple ledger anchors enrollment, the echo verification step records each proof, and the willow bond vault finalizes penalties.
